summary.text: Andy Ellis, a Baltimore resident and a volunteer leader of the Maryland Green Party for a decade, lost the November 3, 2026 election for governor of Maryland to Wes Moore.
He had been a candidate for the House of Delegates.

paragraphs.text: Ellis is a Baltimore resident and a former member of the Baltimore City Charter Review Commission.
He was co-chair of the Maryland Green Party and was a candidate for the House of Delegates in 2018.
In 2024 Ellis chaired Baltimore for Democracy, a ballot issue committee formed to oppose a charter amendment on Baltimore City Council size (Question H), which voters defeated.
He became the Green Party's nominee for governor in the party's online nominating primary held July 8 to 22, 2026, with Owen Silverman Andrews, a teacher, as his running mate for lieutenant governor.
During the campaign, his listed priorities included climate and environment emergency declarations, public education funding and reparations.
He received 2.1% of the vote to Wes Moore's 64.1%, according to unofficial results reported by NBC News.
